title: Quarterly cadence for hosted API: model pruning gates, capacity hedges, and OKR mapping
creator: Maya Cortez
description:
Objective: Establish a repeatable quarterly cadence that ties hosted API model catalog pruning and additions to capacity hedges and company OKRs. This ticket defines gating criteria for removing or demoting models, the experiment windows for new model introductions, a cost-capacity buffer policy (capacity hedges), and an OKR-aligned decision matrix so PM/Eng/DS are synchronized each quarter.

Why now: Demand patterns across hosted endpoints have become more volatile. We must reduce catalogue sprawl (reducing maintenance and evaluation surface) while preserving coverage for critical customer cohorts. Aligning pruning and capacity decisions with OKRs ensures the fleet supports current business priorities (conversions, latency SLOs, and token-cost reductions).

Deliverables:
- Pruning gate definition (health score thresholds, minimum traffic, eval regression limits).
- Capacity hedge policy (reserved headroom by tier, burst budgets, auto-fallback routing to variants).
- Quarterly cadence playbook (timeline, owner roster, intake template, rollouts/canary windows).
- OKR mapping sheet linking each catalog action to a measurable OKR signal (e.g., retention lift, cost/token reduction, latency p50).
- Monitoring/Alerting checklist for regression detection tied to canary windows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pruning gates documented and approved by PM + Runtime Eng + Applied ML.
- Capacity hedge policy validated with SRE and Finance; simulated on last quarter's traffic spike scenario.
- Playbook published in Confluence with templates and a recurring calendar entry for quarterly cadence.
- Two pilot pruning decisions executed in a canary window with no customer-impacting regressions.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Aggressive pruning reduces ops load but may remove niche model variants that drive high-LTV flows; mitigation: minimum cohort traffic + fallback policy.
- Capacity hedges cost money (reserved capacity) vs. outage risk; mitigation: tiered hedges + burst policies and cross-region fallbacks.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Maya Cortez (owner), Product Leads for Hosted API
- Runtime/Serving Eng: SLO owners for latency/cost (ENG-1842 contact)
- Applied ML: model health metrics and eval gating
- SRE/Finance: capacity hedge validation and budget sign-off
- Developer Experience: communicate deprecations and new variants to integrators

Timeline (Q1):
- Week 1-2: Draft gating criteria and capacity hedge sketch (complete)
- Week 3-4: Cross-functional review and simulation with SRE/Finance
- Week 5-7: Pilot two pruning actions behind canary windows
- Week 8: Post-pilot review and playbook publication
- Week 9+: Rollout cadence and integrate into quarterly planning rituals

Artifacts:
- Confluence: /display/PM/Quarterly+Catalog+Cadence+2026 (draft)
- Spreadsheet: OKR mapping & model health score workbook (link in comments)
- Simulation notebook: github.com/redwood-inference/sim-capacity-hedge PR#214

Open decisions:
- Exact health score weighting between model latency regressions and quality drop (precision/recall)
- Minimum cohort size threshold for pruning (proposal: 0.05% of monthly traffic)

Risks:
- False-positive pruning due to short-term traffic dips; addressed by requiring two-week stability window.
- Over-provisioning hedges will increase unit costs; require Finance threshold for tolerated reserve spend.
